Hi all — I ran a quick pass on acme_context_profile.csv. Summary of profiling (sample-level estimates):
- Mean prompt tokens: 472
- Median prompt tokens: 210 (heavy right tail)
- Mean completion tokens: 370
- 8k-context needs: ~72% of sessions fit comfortably (with standard truncation/batching)
- 32k-context needs: ~18% of sessions need extended context (documents, thread history, or full user paste)
- 128k-context needs: ~10% are true long-doc cases (full legal/medical docs, long transcripts)

Implications for pricing and serving:
- Unit economics baseline (model equivalent to an open Llama-family medium-large): we can target a preliminary ballpark of $15–$25 per 1M tokens at 8k (includes infra, caching, and amortized engineering).
- For 32k context windows expect a multiplier of ~1.6–2.0x on a per-token basis (due to memory/KV pressure, reduced batching efficiency).
- For 128k expect a ~3.5–5x multiplier unless you shard or pre-chunk documents and do retrieval augmentation.

I'll attach the raw token distribution slices and a sample cost calc that maps your stated band ($2k–$10k/month) to likely monthly throughput (tokens/month) across the different context sizes.

Notes/assumptions:
- Estimates assume 90th percentile latency SLOs for interactive flows. Batch/offline jobs would drop unit costs substantially.
- We assumed a 60% cache/prefix reuse for conversational flows — if your flows have little repetition the effective cost per useful token rises.

Dev
Applied ML / Inference Engineering

Alex — great questions. I've put together a short pricing table (see below) to help convert budget bands into token volumes and user/session assumptions. I'll also attach an updated PDF with latency tiers and recommendations for mixing interactive + batch workloads. High-level table (assume $/1M token = midpoint numbers below):

- Baseline (8k context) unit price: $20 / 1M tokens
  - $2,000/month -> 100M tokens/month
  - $5,000/month -> 250M tokens/month
  - $10,000/month -> 500M tokens/month

- 32k context (1.8x multiplier): effective $/1M tokens = $36
  - $2,000 -> ~55.6M tokens/month
  - $5,000 -> ~138.9M tokens/month
  - $10,000 -> ~277.8M tokens/month

- 128k context (4x multiplier): effective $/1M tokens = $80
  - $2,000 -> 25M tokens/month
  - $5,000 -> 62.5M tokens/month
  - $10,000 -> 125M tokens/month

Example user/session mapping (illustrative):
- If avg session = 900 tokens total (prompt+completion) and 3 sessions/user/day -> ~2.7k tokens/user/day -> ~81k tokens/user/month (~30 days).
  - At 8k baseline price $20/1M: $2,000 buys ~1,234 users/month (100M / 81k)
  - At 32k effective price $36/1M: $2,000 buys ~686 users/month

Latency & tier recommendations:
- Interactive features (median latency target <300ms): prefer 8k or 32k with optimized batching and KV caching. 32k can hit <300ms for most requests if you accept slightly higher infra footprint (larger GPUs / memory) and reduced batching per-GPU.
- 128k long-docs: recommend batch processing or retrieval-augmented chunking. If you must serve interactive 128k at <300ms, we need dedicated capacity (higher reserved cost) and that will push per-token economics toward the 3.5–5x range Dev mentioned.

Next steps:
- I'll turn this into a short one-pager with the tables and a recommended starter config (Dedicated small pool + batch queue). Jordan / Dev — can you add a recommended GPU flavor and estimated reserved capacity to the one-pager?
- Alex / Priya — if you can confirm the percent of traffic that will be batch vs interactive, we'll produce a tuned proposal.

Can we schedule 30 mins next Tue (4/20) to review the one-pager?

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
